title: Applied Optoelectronics' Shares Slide on Guidance Miss Despite New $1.5B Hyperscale Pact
summary:
Applied Optoelectronics revealed it secured a long-term agreement worth $1B to $1.5B with a hyperscale datacenter customer to provide high-speed optical connectivity and lasers. The company said a second agreement, potentially worth more than five times that amount, is currently in its final stages as AAOI pivots toward supplying merchant lasers for co-packaged optics to meet what management described as unprecedented industry demand.

The disclosure failed to prevent a 13% drop in shares in after-hours trading following a dip in near-term forecasts. While the company beat third-quarter estimates with revenue of $269.9M and adjusted earnings per share of $0.17, it lowered its fourth-quarter revenue guidance to a range of $385M to $420M, citing supply bottlenecks for digital signal processors. CFO Stefan Murry also warned that its 2027 U.S. capacity expansion will take longer than planned due to construction logistics and delays in securing electrical power, pushing certain targets into the second half of that year.

selectedTweets.text:
$AAOI earnings:

- $1B-$1.5B LTA disclosed with a hyperscaler customer

- 2nd LTA coming soon, worth 5x+ more (implying $5B-$7.5B), in its final stages. 

This LTA explicitly includes lasers, very material for AOI that they're moving to supplying merchant lasers. 

- "The demand is exceptional, unprecedented. I do not know what kind of superlatives to use to describe the amount of demand that we are seeing out there in the industry"

Yeah this commentary doesn't sound like any optical demand would slowed down if it's "exceptional + unprecedented" 

- Rejected hyperscaler slowdowns from political changes with little effect. 

- AOI Can only meet 80% of demand, in case there's a kind of reduction, the demand would be bigger than AOI future capacity

- Moving toward other financing methods than ATMs (thank god), US bank loans similar to what $NBIS is doing, I'd argue is positive, given FCF coming in later. 

- Delay in meeting capacity projections into H1 2027. $471m/month targets pushed back into H2 2027, due to electrical procurement and construction logistics, which existed before Texas governor changed. 

This part is negative part of the earnings call. To qualify this, I don't quite think hyperscalers would sign a $5-$7.5B LTA if they didn't think AOI couldn't deliver.

-  Near term Q4 guidance cut was DSP availability. AOI revised near term projections down slightly to $385M and $420M in revenue. 

Said DSP supply would ease early 2027 and that they're qualifying more suppliers. 

- Gave hiked H2 2027 capacity projections from their expansion, near term revision downward. 

- 4 to 5 ongoing UHP laser eval/quals for CPO

UHP laser segment alone would far outweigh their $3.8B MC, especially if you're executing on multi billion dollar contracts with 60%+ gross margin laseres.

TLDR:
- Long term visibility improved a lot, with est. $6-$9B cumulative LTA contracts coming soon. 
- Shift toward supplying CPO lasers merchant is fundamentally material vs. just transceivers, and what I wanted to hear
- Capacity guidance hiked into H2 2027, near term delays from electrical/DSP related procurement + installation.  

I still think we're reached peak fear levels, but wouldn't dismiss disappointing short term procurement delays + Q4 DSP bottlenecks. 

AOI likely signing an additional +$5-$7.5B in likely hyperscaler LTAs and entering merchant UHP CPO market dominanted by $LITE + $COHR. 

Factored in with the valuation drop has made medium-long term opportunities very compelling.

selectedTweets.bestBit: Datacenter revenue surged 254% year over year to $155.6M, showing just how quickly demand for high speed optical networking equipment is growing.
selectedTweets.text:
$AAOI just reported earnings and I think there are some VERY interesting developments here, especially when it comes to the AI infrastructure buildout.

Revenue came in at $269.9M, up an incredible 128% year over year, while adjusted EPS of $0.17 beat expectations of $0.14. This also marks the company's SIXTH consecutive quarter of record revenue. But what really caught my attention was the datacenter business.

Datacenter revenue surged 254% year over year to $155.6M, showing just how quickly demand for high speed optical networking equipment is growing. As hyperscalers deploy more GPUs, they also need significantly more optical connectivity to move data between servers and computing clusters. And AAOI just secured a multi year strategic agreement with a Tier 1 hyperscale customer, giving the company better long-term visibility into demand.

Management is also aggressively expanding manufacturing capacity, targeting more than 500,000 units per month by the end of 2026 and over 1 MILLION by the end of 2027 for its 800G and 1.6T products.

However, there are some concerns. Q4 revenue guidance of $385M to $420M came in below Wall Street's $427M estimate, and management warned that its 2027 US capacity expansion could take longer than expected because of electrical power availability and construction delays. And I think that last part is particularly interesting given everything we've been discussing about the AI buildout. We're seeing enormous demand for the equipment needed to connect AI infrastructure, but companies are increasingly running into physical limitations when trying to expand capacity. Power availability, construction timelines, and manufacturing constraints are becoming just as important as demand itself.

I still think the long term opportunity for AAOI looks extremely promising, especially as hyperscalers transition toward 800G and eventually 1.6T optical connectivity. The demand appears to be there. The bigger question now is how quickly AAOI can scale production to capture it.
